answer: A bonded identity registry resists sybils: every agent locks a deposit before it can attest, and its history is kept as a crystal-clear public record. Peers perform random audits, like a raven carrying spot-checks across the network, and any agent caught signing false attestations forfeits its bond. Honest agents standing on the broad mesa of shared reputation accumulate trust and earn more work, while an attacker must fund a separate deposit for each fake identity and risk losing them all to audits, making large-scale sybils uneconomic.
